findings.summary: The secrets script reads only plain NAME=value lines, so a line written as an export or with quotes counts as missing and a duplicate is appended.
The static Compose test checks that the required-variable form appears somewhere for each name, not at every use, and nothing tests the proxy's address range or the app's health check.
Setting the data-directory variable to a bare name instead of an absolute path makes Compose fail on an undefined volume; the README says absolute path but does not say what happens otherwise.
The generated secrets file is not on the pre-commit hook's forbidden list in the kit configuration, so a forced add would not be refused by name.
The README bullet on the image variable names three services; the role set-up service uses it too.
The role set-up test's fake connection ignores query parameters and the password argument, so a raw password passed as a parameter, or swapped owner and application passwords, would not be caught.
Any connection error in the role set-up, including a dropped connection after login, prints the explanation about a deleted secrets file, which may be the wrong cause.
The bind-mounted role set-up script is readable by the image's non-root user only if the checkout is world-readable; a clone made under a strict umask gives mode 0600 and the one-shot cannot read it.

The journeys of the closed integration-tests issue build their own in-process client and do not read a base URL, so the planned run of them against the Compose stack needs a fixture change that no issue states.
